On a hybrid recurrent model, every cached recurrent-state checkpoint costs

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Mark the session dead when its ConnectAck send fails
items.author: nilig
items.summary: clears the pending registration before sending. If that send raises, the exception escapes and the local session remains alive. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

`P2PSession._poll_registration` clears the pending registration before sending `ConnectAckMsg`. If that send raises, the exception escapes `poll()` and the local session remains alive. Route the ack through `_do_send` so a send exception marks the local connection dead and allows the manager to reap its pending work.

Part of #63602 (gap 5).

## Claims

- A raised `ConnectAckMsg` send error marks the local connection dead instead of escaping `poll()`.
- The manager can reap that session and fail its pending local work without waiting for the request deadline, provided polling an

items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`ChatCompletionRequest` accepts `thinking_token_budget` and passes it to `SamplingParams`, but `ResponsesRequest` (`/v1/responses`) has no such field, so the value is ignored there (unknown fields are allowed and only logged at debug level).

As a result, a deployment that caps thinking with `thinking_token_budget` gets the cap on `/v1/chat/completions` but not on `/v1/responses`. Clients that only speak the Responses API (for example apps built on the Vercel AI SDK's OpenAI provider, which calls `/responses` by default) cannot cap thinking at all.

items.author: zheyuf
items.summary: MiniMax-M3's sparse indexer caches one 128-dim index key per token in each of its 57 sparse layers, and every TP rank keeps all of it. With FP8 index-K that is 7,296 B per token per GPU: 28% of a rank's KV bytes at TP2 and 44% at TP4/TP8.
items.body:
## Description

MiniMax-M3's sparse indexer caches one 128-dim index key per token in each of its 57 sparse layers, and every TP rank keeps all of it. With FP8 index-K that is 7,296 B per token per GPU: 28% of a rank's KV bytes at TP2 and 44% at TP4/TP8.

This PR adds `indexer_kv_dtype: nvfp4`. Index-K is stored as NVFP4 (E2M1 values, one E4M3 scale per 16 dims) whose scales are restricted to {1, 1.25, 1.5} x 2^e, so every dequantized value is exactly an E4M3 value. - **Fused:** one `MoEAllReduce` kernel does finalize, all-reduce, residual add and RMSNorm.

## Motivation

Kimi K3 inference on Ascend can still depend on CPU sequence-length mirrors in both the MLA target and DSpark draft attention paths. Maintaining these mirrors and updating host-side graph inputs introduces synchronization overhead on the decode critical path.

Removing this dependency requires both target and draft attention to consume valid KV lengths directly from device memory. This PR enables that flow for supported configurations, while preserving CPU mirrors for attention paths that still require host metadata.

## Modifications

- Add opt-in CANN FlashMLA support

## Motivation

Large JSON request bodies (for example base64-encoded multimodal inputs) can exceed default HTTP/1.1 parser limits in Uvicorn and Granian, causing failed requests before they reach application code. Issue #6622 asks for a server flag to raise this limit.

- Add `--max-payload-size` to serving CLI arguments (default 10 MiB / 10485760 bytes).
- Wire the limit into all HTTP server launch paths in `http_server.py` (Granian + Uvicorn, including multi-worker).
- Document the flag in `server_arguments.mdx`.

Fixes #6622

items.title: [RFC]: Bring vLLM's development cost back to linear: a small core with owned, independently tested components
items.author: aijanai
items.summary: Proposes restructuring vLLM into a small engine core plus independently owned and tested components to reduce coupling and linearize development costs.
items.body:
### Motivation.

Every new model, kernel, platform or quantization method in vLLM lands in the same tree, the same review queue and the same CI. Because components import each other directly, the cost of a change grows with the number of pairs that can interact, not with the number of components: development cost grows much faster than the codebase. items.title: [Bugfix][PP] Filter KV-cache tensors to worker-owned layers
items.author: ebfio
items.summary: Fixes pipeline-parallel KV-cache tensor emission so only worker-owned layers are included, preventing StopIteration crashes when a rank owns no layers in a group.
items.body:
Fixes #63615.

Emits KV-cache tensors only for layers the worker actually owns, so the `next()` lookup in `allocate_kv_cache` (`worker/utils.py`) always matches under PP. When a pipeline rank owns none of a group's layers, the worker-side projection keeps the group's global `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` unfiltered while emptying its `layer_names`; the planner loop then iterates the unfiltered spec and emits tensors naming other ranks' layers, and the consumer-side lookup raises a bare `StopIteration` — surfacing on the *other* rank as an opaque `Worker failed` error (full analysis in the issue).

items.title: allocate_kv_cache raises StopIteration when a PP rank owns none of a KV group's layers
items.author: ebfio
items.summary: Under pipeline parallelism, a rank that holds none of a KV-cache group's layers can still be handed naming layers owned by other ranks. The lookup in (, filtering ) then finds no group and raises a bare — which surfaces on the other rank as an opaque.
items.body:
Under pipeline parallelism, a rank that holds none of a KV-cache group's layers can still be handed `kv_cache_tensors` naming layers owned by other ranks. The lookup in `allocate_kv_cache` (`vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`, `group_id, group = next(...)` filtering `layer_name in group.layer_names`) then finds no group and raises a bare `StopIteration` — which surfaces on the *other* rank as an opaque `RuntimeError: Worker failed with error ''`. That opacity is why nobody has filed this: the real stack is on the rank that died.

**Reproduction:** DeepSeek V4.1 (NVIDIA tree), PP2 with the default 20/20
discussion: Fix proposed in #63617 (planner-side filter, with a test reproducing the failing state red/green). For context, the deployment that hit this runs DeepSeek V4.1 + DSpark under PP2 — the enablement is #63619, which depends on the KV fix.

items.author: bandham-manikanta
items.summary: Fixes a missing cp.async.wait_group barrier in hadacore kernel for odd row counts during INT4 per-token-head KV cache rotation, preventing silent data corruption and CUDA crashes.
items.body:
Fixes #63514

### Problem
When using INT4 per-token-head KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype int4_per_token_head`), `reshape_and_cache_int4` rotates Key and Value tensors via `hadacore_transform`. 

For `head_dim = 256`, `num_chunks` is 2. When the row count (`num_tokens * num_kv_heads_per_rank`) is odd, the last warp receives only 1 chunk (`real_num_chunks = 1`).

`diff_num_chunks` was calculated as:
```cpp
int64_t diff_num_chunks = real_num_chunks - num_chunks; // 1 - 2 = -1
```

items.body:
# [Perf] paged-experts: fewer host syncs in host-planned steps

## Motivation

This PR aims to decrease TTFT.

Currently, Paged Experts (#42557) plans a step on the host when it routes more entries than the K resident slots: prefill, and decode batches past `K // top_k`. Such a step runs in waves, and each MoE layer syncs with the GPU 6 times plus once per wave (twice on the compacted Marlin path): two reads of the device LRU state, `torch.unique().tolist()`, a blocking upload of each wave's slot map, a `nonzero()` per compacted wave, `step.item()`, and two blocking uploads of the state back.

# [Perf] paged-experts: exact size pinning

## Motivation

This PR aims to decrease memory footprint.

Currently, the Paged Experts Feature (#42557) keeps every expert of the model in page-locked host memory. torch's pinned allocator rounds each allocation up to a power of two, so **a 402 MB `w13` tensor pins 512 MiB**. Across a model this pins about a third more than the experts need on Qwen3-30B-A3B, and 85% more on gpt-oss-20b. Pinned memory cannot be swapped, and it is often what decides whether a model fits: WSL2, for example, caps it at about half of RAM.

items.author: wujingyue

- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Previously, `fully_shard_context` was an alias for `FsdpContext`, coupling construction-scope management with runtime state that persists throughout training. These responsibilities have different reasons to change: construction controls which context new modules join, while runtime behavior controls communication streams and prefetching. Separating them follows Robert C. Martin's [Single Responsibility Principle](https://blog.cleancoder.com/uncle-bob/2014/05/08/SingleReponsibilityPrinciple.html)

Public video frames are uint8, but two return paths move the full FP32 clip to the host and quantize it afterwards:

## Motivation

Large local diffusion replies are spilled to a private `.npy` file in the request's shared-memory directory. When the client materializes the reply, `NumpyArrayFileRef.materialize` calls `np.load`, which reads the whole payload into a second host allocation before the file is unlinked. A 124-frame 1344x768 video reply carries about 1.54 GB of FP32 data through this path.

## Modifications

- `NumpyArrayFileRef.materialize` loads the spill with `mmap_mode="c"` and returns a plain `np.ndarray` view over the mapping. Pages are read when the consumer touches them instead of up front

items.author: arathi-hlab
items.summary: Fixes a crash on Intel XPU by skipping the CustomAllReduceV2 import in dp_attention.py, avoiding a missing tvm_ffi dependency.
items.body:
## Motivation

#46138 added a module-level `from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce_v2 import CustomAllReduceV2` to `dp_attention.py`. `custom_all_reduce_v2` imports `sglang/kernels/ops/communication/all_reduce.py`, which does `import tvm_ffi` at module level. `tvm_ffi` is not installed in the XPU image (`intel/sglang-dev:latest`), and `dp_attention.py` is imported almost everywhere, so importing sglang on XPU now fails. items.author: davidliuk
items.summary: Mixed beam widths need admission accounting in physical request-pool rows. The current gate divides the remaining rows by the incoming candidate's width, then compares that value with the number of staged leaders.
items.body:
## Motivation

Mixed beam widths need admission accounting in physical request-pool rows. The current gate divides the remaining rows by the incoming candidate's width, then compares that value with the number of staged leaders. With a four-row pool, `[4, 1]` can therefore admit five rows and fail when the beam spawns. Conversely, an eight-row pool can reject the final group in `[2, 1, 4]` even though all seven rows fit.

A stop token selected on the final allowed beam step also loses its stop reason, causing it to be reported as length-finished and retained in decoded text.

`fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` applies inverse RoPE to the attention output and quantizes it to block FP8 for `wo_a`. It launched one single-warp program per (token, head), which ran at 1.5 TB/s on B200 and took 8.6% of a 16k-token DeepSeek-V4-Flash prefill step (TP2).

This documentation-only PR proposes an SGLang serving primitive for active incremental prompt ingestion: append prompt chunks to one in-flight request, prefill each committed chunk, and delay decoding until an explicit finalize operation.

This is intended for producer-consumer workloads where prompt tokens arrive from another model, tool, parser, retriever, or streaming service.

- Distinction from response streaming, chunked prefill, session-aware radix cache, and incremental chat tokenization.

## Motivation

After a decode OOM retraction, a retracted request is re-admitted by re-prefilling its prompt plus the tokens it already generated. Admission then reserves its full `max_new_tokens` of decode headroom again, so those tokens are counted twice. Block files in the `fs` tier are named by content hash, so when a prefix that is already on disk gets stored again, `_store_block` skips the write. This PR makes the tier report only the blocks it actually wrote.

## Claims

- `transfer_bytes` now counts written blocks only, and is `0` when every block was already on disk. `BackpressureDetector.update` already ignores `num_bytes <= 0`, so these jobs stop

items.body:
## Motivation

An RL weight sync runs `pause_generation` in retract mode, then `update_weights_*` with `flush_cache=True`, then `continue_generation`. The flush queues AllBlocksCleared, but a paused scheduler never publishes KV events, so a KV-event router (sgl-router, or Dynamo) keeps that worker's whole pre-flush cache view for the entire sync and scores requests against blocks that no longer exist. The clear reaches the router only after resume.

#24003 added a publish at pause entry. It covers what was queued up to the pause, not what happens during it, such as the weight update's flush.

items.title: [Bugfix] Propagate EngineDeadError on AsyncLLM output_handler cancellation
items.author: PratikCreates
items.summary: Fixes AsyncLLM output_handler not propagating EngineDeadError on asyncio.CancelledError, which previously caused active request collectors to hang indefinitely during shutdown.
items.body:
## Overview
Notify active request collectors with EngineDeadError when the background output_handler task is cancelled in AsyncLLM.

## Motivation & Behavior Change
- In Python 3.8+, asyncio.CancelledError derives from BaseException so it bypassed the \except Exception\ block in \output_handler\.
- When \output_handler\ is cancelled (e.g., during \AsyncLLM.shutdown()\ or worker cancellation), active request collectors never received an error notification and remained blocked indefinitely on \^Gwait self.ready.wait()\.
- **Behavior change**: Pending requests now fail fast with \EngineDeadError\

items.title: Checkpoint domains for multi-site training
items.author: nick-knight
items.summary: Megatron's default checkpointing logic may fail when training across multiple sites. The checkpoint files will be scattered across the different sites' filesystems (in the same-named path on each), guaranteeing at least one on checkpoint load.
items.body:
Megatron's default checkpointing logic may fail when training across multiple sites. The checkpoint files will be scattered across the different sites' filesystems (in the same-named path on each), guaranteeing at least one `FileNotFoundError` on checkpoint load. (See below for a more concrete example.) 

This PR adds "checkpoint domains" to Megatron's distributed checkpointing API. A checkpoint domain scopes save/load collectives and shard writer/reader selection to a supplied process group. By setting these domains to reflect site localities, callers can avoid the aforementioned problem.

## Overview

In multi-turn P/D serving, the next turn's prompt starts with the previous prompt plus the tokens the decoder just generated. Only the decoder has that KV, so the prefiller recomputes it every turn. items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-

After the indexer scores a MiniMax-M3 context chunk, each (token, index head) row picks its 16 highest-scoring 128-token blocks. `minimax_m3_select_blocks` reads each row on its own, strided by the token count, because the scores are stored token-contiguous. items.title: [https://nvbugs/6900756][perf] KVCMv2: fill the initial host tier in parallel, populate in 4 MiB calls
items.author: thorjohnsen
items.summary:
A KVCMv2 host tier is filled by one worker thread per. It goes 512 MiB at a time: the step open, prefault it with one call, then register it. [Discussion: 🎉
ℹ️ Recent review info
<]
items.body:
## Description

A KVCMv2 host tier is filled by one worker thread per `HostMem`. It goes 512 MiB at a time: `mprotect` the step open, prefault it with one `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` call, then register it. This PR changes two things:

1. **Prefault in 4 MiB calls (every fill).** A `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` call holds the process's `mmap_lock` for reading until it returns. Everything that needs the lock for writing waits behind it: the other pool's `mprotect` and registrations, and allocations on the executor. One call per 512 MiB step makes those waits long.
2. **Prefault the initial fill in parallel.*

## Summary

Adds an opt-in `token_order: morton` knob to `SolAttentionConfig`. Sol-Attn routes per 64-token block over the flattened video sequence; in Wan's native T-H-W raster order a block is a run along width (on the 720p grid a 64-token block spans 73 tokens along W and 1 row along H), so routing decisions have weak 3D locality. With Morton (Z-order) ordering each block covers a compact ~4x4x4 neighborhood (mean per-block extent 3.0 x 3.4 x 3.9 on the (21, 45, 80) grid). Fix `NIXLCheckpointEngine.build_topology` for a topology with one rollout worker.

items.title: fix: run dense fused kernels through the FSDP2 LM head
items.author: ZiyiXu06
items.summary: Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads, including models such as Qwen3. Previously, the fused forward accessed directly, bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular Tensors with DTensors during matrix multipl…
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

items.title: fix(rm_hub): accept numeric zero ground truth in grade_answer_verl
items.author: Domin-Focus
items.summary: Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct response scores 0 under. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.
items.body:
## Problem

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

```python
if not ground_truth:
    return False
ground_truth = str(ground_truth)
```

Labels are passed through from the dataset as-is (`slime/utils/data.py:272`), so a zero answer arrives as `0` or `0.0`. Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct `\boxed{0}` response scores 0 under `rm_type=math`. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`ReplayBuffer._wait_for_next_poll()` sleeps a hard-coded `poll_interval=2.0` between TransferQueue metadata syncs (used
by both the sync `sample()` and the async `wait_for_sampleable()`). The trainer therefore notices the last finished
prompt up to 2 s late, and `timing_s/gen` is quantized to multiples of 2 s (main, vLLM: 2.21, 4.21, 4.21, 2.21 … s;
SGLang: 2.28 s every step). This PR replaces the sleep with a wait on a small completion counter that rollout workers
bump when a prompt reaches a terminal status. On 8x MI355X GSM8K GRPO it cuts `timing_s/gen` by 22–31%

### What does this PR do?

Megatron's `optimizer_cpu_offload=True` turns the optimizer into a **HybridDeviceOptimizer (HDO)**: it permanently splits optimizer state between CPU memory and GPU memory via `optimizer_offload_fraction`. # What does this PR do?

With context parallelism, running a shorter sequence after a longer one can reuse the wrong YaRN positions and change the model's output. The cache contains positions already split between CP ranks. For CP2 rank 0, length 64 caches positions `0…15, 48…63`, but length 32 needs `0…7, 24…31`. Taking a prefix of the old cache gives the wrong positions.

Rebuild the cache when a non-packed sequence shrinks with CP > 1. CP1 and packed inputs can still reuse the cache.

# What does this PR do?
Unit tests in CI have intermittent hangs, most notably in the GDN unit tests, but also in other test suites more rarely.

This is due to [pytorch#200848](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/200848). torch >= 2.10 forks worker processes, and locks break under forking in Python < 3.12.8 or Python 3.13.0.

The fix is setting `TORCHINDUCTOR_QUIESCE_ASYNC_COMPILE_POOL=0`. This PR does that, and also undoes various previous patches meant to work around this issue.

items.title: fix(inference): promote TorchSampling temperature divisor to FP32
items.author: muditagrawal2007
items.summary: Fixes the temperature-scaling precision bug in #7857, and fixes an in-place mutation of the caller's logits that the first fix introduced. divided logits by the temperature in the input's dtype.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Fixes the `TorchSampling` temperature-scaling precision bug in #7857, and fixes an in-place mutation of the caller's logits that the first fix introduced.

`TorchSampling.filter_logits` divided logits by the temperature **in the input's dtype**. For BF16/FP16 logits that (a) loses precision in the scaled logit and shifts top-p nucleus membership at moderate temperatures, and (b) overflows FP16 at `temperature=0` (the divisor is floored to `MIN_SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE=1e-6`, so `logits * 1e6` → `inf`)

items.summary: / decide whether an experimental API has reached its end of life by comparing only the minor component of the version: Once mcore crosses a major boundary and the minor version resets to 0, this comparison can never fire again, so expired experimental APIs sil…
items.body:
`experimental_fn` / `experimental_cls` decide whether an experimental API has reached its end of life by comparing only the *minor* component of the version:

```python
PkgVersion(introduced_with_version).minor + max_lifetime < PkgVersion(mcore_version).minor
```

Once mcore crosses a major boundary and the minor version resets to 0, this comparison can never fire again, so expired experimental APIs silently stop being flagged. ## Root cause

#2585 added the zeroing to keep padding tokens out of FP8 amax

items.title: [vllm, rollout] fix: honor teacher temperature in on-policy distillation
items.author: yph22
items.summary: Honor when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation. Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

## 背景

此 PR 添加了一个**跨仓库自动文档翻译工作流**（`schedule_doc_translate_ascend.yaml`），它能自动将 `docs/ascend_tutorial/zh/` 下的中文文档翻译为 `docs/ascend_tutorial/en/` 下的英文文档，并按周计划执行。


## 工作原理

此工作流在 `verl-project/verl` 仓库中运行，并使用**独立的私有 Fork 仓库**来存储翻译工具（Python 翻译引擎、技能/提示文档以及 `.po` 翻译记忆库）。这使得上游仓库保持整洁——它仅接收 `en/` 文档和工作流文件的更改。

**工作流步骤：**

1. **检出（Checkout）** Fork 私有仓库的 `main` 分支（包含 `translate_md.py`、`skill.md`、`.po` 缓存）。
2. **同步（Sync）** Fork 的 `main` 分支与最新的上游 `main` 分支（通过 `git merge`），然后将同步后的 `main` 分支推送回 Fork。
3. **翻译（Translate）** — 运行 `translate_md.py`，将每个中文文档拆分为块，复用 `.po` 文件中的缓存翻译，仅对更改/未翻译的块调用 OpenAI 兼容的

items.title: [tool, rollout] fix: create BaseTool instances once per trajectory and release them when it ends
items.author: nataliekung
items.summary: runs, and for every tool call. A therefore cannot keep state from one turn to the next, although is documented as creating "a tool instance for a trajectory" and points to for per-trajectory state such as sandbox VMs, scratch directories and DB rows.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`ToolAgentLoop._call_tool` runs `create`, `execute` and `release` for every tool call. A `BaseTool` therefore cannot keep state from one turn to the next, although `BaseTool.create` is documented as creating "a tool instance for a trajectory" and `docs/sglang_multiturn/multiturn.rst` points to `BaseTool` for per-trajectory state such as sandbox VMs, scratch directories and DB rows.

This PR creates the instance on the first call to a tool, reuses it for the rest of the trajectory, and releases every instance once when the trajectory ends, including when it raises.

items.title: [Bug] Startup health polling can block on an unresponsive server
items.author: LinzeShi
items.summary: If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach. This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. [Discussion: independent check on main: this no longer reproduces.]
items.body:
### Bug Description

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. The expected behavior is to bound each probe, then check process liveness and retry while the process is alive. The overall startup wait should remain unbounded for slow model loading.

### Steps to Reproduce

## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.summary: OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes, not the matched-temperature objective. Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to …
items.body:
## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to `1.0` only makes the mismatched behavior explicit. Supporting the real-temperature case requires changing the SGLang input-logprob path.

This lowers Draft-token acceptance and average acceptance length, and may
eventually make the additional Draft and verification cost larger than the speculative-decoding benefit.

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. ## Description

Fixes #304

Importing any `rm_hub` submodule executes `vime/rollout/rm_hub/__init__.py`, which imports runtime-only deps at module level, so the reward CPU tests fail at pytest collection in lightweight environments. The chain is deeper than the issue's traceback shows: `aiohttp` (used by `remote_rm` only), `vime.utils.misc` / `vime.utils.types` (pull in `torch` and `httpx`), and `sympy` / `pylatexenc` at the top of `math_utils`.

## Changes

- `rm_hub/__init__.py`: defer `aiohttp` and `load_function` to their call sites; move `Sample` / `aiohttp` under `TYPE_CHECKING`

This PR adds an optional rollout data transfer path for **disaggregated training** (separate rollout and actor GPUs). When enabled, vime transfers rollout tensors (`tokens`, `loss_masks`) through **Mooncake Store** instead of the Ray object store.

This is useful when rollout and training run on different GPUs or nodes and you want a dedicated high-bandwidth transfer layer rather than serializing large tensors through Ray.

Ported from [slime PR #1709](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/1709).

Replace the pause/resume-based rollout abort with a **delete-type** abort, so that under `--partial-rollout` the long tail is **truncated to partial** (and resumable next step) instead of either deadlocking or running to completion.
